correctness.rationale: Source Section 3.1 definitions exactly match the proof. Every × cube image is a clique of the two-section graph, giving an integral basiswise identification. The explicitly defined highest-one-coordinate corner cube is a nondegenerate chain map: zero faces omit vertices, first one-face omits v0, and all higher one-faces are degenerate. On a full simplex the last-coordinate cone is an explicit normalized integral contraction. Cube bases obey the degreewise split inclusion/exclusion sequence under unions. Induction on the number of faces and the homology long exact sequences prove the all-degree integral comparison without numerical extrapolation. A standalone checker tested 20,874 normalized cubes and the signed identities, with mod-two H0/H1 comparison as independent finite crosscheck.

value.rationale: An entire recently proposed integral hypergraph homology theory is structurally identified in all degrees with a classical calculable flag-complex invariant. The explicit comparison exhibits exactly the loss of higher-hyperedge data beyond the 2-section, gives direct access to all-degree torsion/persistence via simplicial chains, and delineates a meaningful limitation of the newly proposed theory. This is neither a routine finite table nor an arbitrary narrow invariant.
